StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). StackType's only non-presentation readers are GetTypeForAmount (PowerModel.cs:462) and InvokePowerModified's VFX split (Creature.cs:628). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterModifyingHpLostAfterOsty.rationale: IntangiblePower.cs:35-39 is Flash() only. Presentation. Note the sim DOES have the machinery this would need (hooks.py:149-154 after_modify_hp_lost, used by BufferPower), so this is a deliberate no-op rather than a missing hook.

guards.issue: The sim has no combat-phase guard on any modifier hook. This is the power-level face of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's structural gap G6 (no IsEnding/CanReceivePowers backstop) and of hook_dispatch's gap G8 (no IsOverOrEnding gate on combat dispatches); per binding rule 3 it carries the same `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Recorded here because Intangible is the only ported power that spells the guard out itself, so a reader comparing the two files sees a real missing line rather than an architectural absence. DORMANT for the same reason hook_dispatch G8 is: everything reachable on that path is combat-scoped state the combat then discards. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:375 and :370 both test `target is self.owner`. C# returns the unmodified amount / decimal.MaxValue for a non-owner; the sim returns `amount` / None, and hooks.py:80-93 folds None out of the cap min. Equivalent.
powers.py:383 `min(amount, 1)` gives the same answer for every amount: below 1 it returns the amount unchanged, at or above 1 it returns 1. Exact rather than merely equivalent.

powers.py:387 calls _tick (powers.py:70-75), not _tick_duration -- so Intangible does NOT honour SkipNextDurationTick, matching C#'s use of the plain Decrement. Getting this right is the whole point of the sim having two tick verbs, and Intangible is on the correct one; contrast Vulnerable/Weak/Frail, which use TickDownDuration on both sides.

powers.py:386 on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345) fires unconditionally once per enemy side end for every listener, which is exactly the C# shape -- an Intangible on the PLAYER also ticks at the enemy side's end. This is one of the rare AfterSideTurnEnd overrides where the sim is in the right slot for both owners.

guards.what: The double implementation (ModifyHpLost + ModifyDamageCap) is reproduced
guards.rationale: C#'s own comments (IntangiblePower.cs:41-45, :55-58) say the cap arm exists for block loss and damage previews while the HP arm does the real work; the sim ports both (powers.py:363-384) with the same split and the same comments.
